messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] FindDupMarkers output
parts:
As it says in the help file, the output of findDupMarkers is list of marker names; each component is a set of markers whose genotypes match [each other and] one other marker, and the name of the component is the name of the marker that they match.

For example:

data(hyper)
findDupMarkers(hyper)

Gives the output:

$D4Mit53
[1] "D4Mit89"

$D4Mit80
[1] "D4Mit81"

$D17Mit57
[1] "D17Mit113"

$D17Mit23
[1] "D17Mit45"

D4Mit89 is duplicate of D4Mit53; D4Mit81 is a duplicate of D4Mit80, etc.

Duplicate markers are grouped together. For each group, one is used as the name of the group, and the others form a component of the output.

In the above output, the duplicate markers are in pairs. As an illustration, we can force a third marker into one of the groups by pasting over its genotype data.

hyper$geno[[4]]$data[,"D4Mit276"] <- hyper$geno[[4]]$data[,"D4Mit80"]
findDupMarkers(hyper)

gives the output

$D4Mit53
[1] "D4Mit89"

$D4Mit81
[1] "D4Mit80" "D4Mit276"

$D17Mit113
[1] "D17Mit57"

$D17Mit45
[1] "D17Mit23"

So now D4Mit81, D4Mit80 and D4Mit276 form a group of three duplicate markers.

karl

On Jul 19, 2012, at 6:06 AM, LisaRC wrote:

> Dear Karl
>
> I am running findDupMarkers but am not sure how to interpret the outputs, and find out exactly which markers have been grouped as identical.
>
> As an example, looking for duplicates on my first chromosome that are adjacent:
>
> dupmar<-findDupMarkers(allmap, 1, exact.only=TRUE, adjacent.only=TRUE)
>
> The output from e.g. ls(dupmar) is something like this:
> [1] "marker 3" "marker 7" "marker 12" "marker 21"
> [5] "marker 33" (etc)
>
> Assuming my markers are numbered in order, does this mean that markers 1 and 2 are not duplicates, but then everything from marker 3 to marker 6 are considered the same? and then from marker 7 to 12? I understand that "One marker (chosen at random) is selected as the name of the group (in the output of the function)" but I am not sure how to see the markers within that group.
>
> Is there a way to find out which markers are grouped together as identical?
>
> (I do expect a lot of these markers to be the same as this is a high density SNP map, so I am trying to eliminate duplicates first, otherwise I run into memory problems).
>
> Many thanks
> Lisa
